qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the City/County Association of Governments of San Mateo County for a supplemental planning project, including submission instructions, deadlines, scope of work, evaluation criteria, and procurement requirements.

quotes.quote:
REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS
 San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning
Project
Date Released: December 19, 2025
Proposals are due: January 23, 2026, 12:00PM PST

The City/County Association of Governments of San Mateo County (C/CAG), a Joint Powers Agency composed of the County of San Mateo and all twenty cities located within San Mateo County, invites qualified consultants to submit proposals for San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project, which is funded through the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) Safe Streets for All (SS4A) Grant Program.
Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026
V. PROPOSAL EVALUATION

findings.title: Proposal Validity Period
findings.fact: The proposal must be a firm offer for a period of 120 days from the due date for proposals.

quotes.quote: Indicate that the proposal is a firm offer to enter into a contract to perform work related to this RFP for a period of 120 days from the due date for proposals.

findings.title: Right to Reject Proposals
findings.fact: C/CAG reserves the right to reject any and all proposals and to waive minor irregularities.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to reject any and all proposals, waive minor irregularities, request additional information, or revisions to offers, negotiate with any or all proposers, and waive any requirements of this RFP when it determines that waiving a requirement is in the best interest of C/CAG.

findings.title: Oral Interviews
findings.fact: The selection process may include oral interviews, and if held, they are evaluated based on presentation and Q&A response criteria.

quotes.quote: The selection process may include oral interviews. If oral interviews are necessary, the consultant will be notified of the time and place of oral interviews and whether any additional information may be required to be submitted. The evaluation criteria for the oral interviews, should they occur, are included below.

8. Presentation by Team (10 points) (if oral interviews are necessary) • Team presentation conveying project understanding, communication skills, innovative ideas, critical issues and solutions. 9. Q&A Response to Panel Questions (10 points) (if oral interviews are necessary) • Proposer provides responses to various interview panel questions.

findings.title: Recommendation for Contract Award
findings.fact: C/CAG may award based on initial proposals without interviews, and reserves the right to negotiate or include a best and final offer stage.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to not convene oral interviews or discussions, and to make an award on the basis of initial proposals. Accordingly, each initial proposal should be submitted on the most favorable terms from a price and a technical viewpoint. C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate and/or include a best and final offer stage to the process.

References may be contacted at any point in the evaluation process. C/CAG reserves the right to consider consultant performance based on comments from submitted references. Experience and ability to perform work is a significant consideration.

findings.title: Selection Disputes
findings.fact: Proposers may protest RFP provisions or selection decisions within specified deadlines.

quotes.quote: A proposer may object to a provision of the RFP on the grounds that it is arbitrary, biased, or unduly restrictive, or to the selection of a particular proposer on the grounds that C/CAG procedures, the provisions of the RFP or applicable provisions of federal, state, or local law have been violated or inaccurately or inappropriately applied by submitting a written protest to the C/CAG Project Manager in accordance with the following deadlines: 1. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due, for objections to RFP provisions. 2. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it did not meet the minimum qualifications or was found to be non-responsive. 3. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date on which the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or, if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later, for objections to the recommended award.

findings.title: Fully Loaded Hourly Rate Definition
findings.fact: Fully loaded hourly rate includes all applicable surcharges such as taxes, insurance, fringe benefits, indirect costs, overhead, profit allowance, and ordinary materials and supplies.

quotes.quote: fully loaded hourly rate means an hourly rate that includes all applicable surcharges such as taxes, insurance and fringe benefits as well as indirect costs, overhead and profit allowance, and ordinary materials and supplies.

findings.title: C/CAG Right to Negotiate or Decline
findings.fact: C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate with or decline to enter into a contract with a proposer whose rates are unreasonable at C/CAG's sole discretion.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate with or to decline to enter into a contract with a proposer whose rates are unreasonable at C/CAG’s sole discretion.

findings.title: Monthly Invoices and Progress Reports
findings.fact: The consultant shall submit monthly invoices and progress reports as part of Task 1 deliverables.

quotes.quote: 4. Monthly Invoices and Progress reports

findings.title: Minimum Qualifications: Three Projects in Past Ten Years
findings.fact: Proposer must demonstrate successful completion of at least three projects in the past ten years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report, Vision Zero Action Plan, or supplemental/implementation planning for Safe Streets for All Grant Program.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory qualification. If the bidder cannot demonstrate three relevant projects, the proposal will be deemed nonresponsive and rejected. The bidder must ensure that the prime or subconsultants collectively meet this requirement.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the firm's project portfolio and identify at least three qualifying projects completed in the last ten years. Prepare detailed descriptions, including client references and outcomes, to include in the proposal. If necessary, partner with subconsultants who have the required experience.

quotes.quote: Proposer must demonstrate to C/CAG’s satisfaction that the prime consultant and/or one or more subconsultant proposed this project have successfully completed at least three (3) projects in the past ten (10) years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report (SSAR), Vision Zero Action Plan and/or supplemental or implementation planning for the Safe Streets for All Grant Program.

findings.title: Minimum Qualifications: Federal Grant Experience
findings.fact: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory qualification. The bidder must prove they have successfully managed large federal grants, including compliance with federal regulations. Failure to demonstrate this could result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Highlight past projects funded by federal grants (e.g., FHWA, FTA, USDOT) in the proposal. Provide specific examples of compliance with federal requirements, such as environmental reviews, labor standards, and reporting. If the firm lacks this experience, consider teaming with a subconsultant who has it.

quotes.quote: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and successfully ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements for such projects.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, via email to Eva Gaye (egaye@smcgov.org) with the subject line 'RFP – San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project'. Proposals received after this time may be considered nonresponsive.
findings.business_implication: Strict deadline and submission method. Late proposals may be rejected. The bidder must ensure timely submission to avoid disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Mark the deadline on calendars and set internal reminders. Prepare the proposal well in advance and submit via email to the specified address with the exact subject line. Confirm receipt with the contact person to avoid any issues.

quotes.quote: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, in accordance with the instructions contained in the RFP. Proposals should be emailed with the subject line “RFP – San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project” to: Eva Gaye (egaye@smcgov.org).
Proposals received after the time and date specified above may be considered nonresponsive.

findings.title: Proposal Format and Page Limit
findings.fact: Proposals must be submitted as one electronic copy in PDF format, with each page 8.5” x 11” or 11” x 17”, sequentially numbered, and include a table of contents. The submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes, relevant experience, and references.
findings.business_implication: The proposal must adhere to strict formatting and page limits. Non-compliance may lead to rejection or negative evaluation. The bidder must carefully manage content within the allowed pages.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan the proposal structure to fit within the 20-page limit. Use the excluded sections (cover letter, title page, TOC, resumes, experience, references) to provide additional information. Ensure all pages are numbered and the PDF is formatted correctly.

quotes.quote: Consultants must submit one (1) electronic copy of the proposal in pdf format. Each page shall be 8.5” x 11” or 11” x 17”. Each page shall be sequentially numbered, and a table of contents shall be provided. Each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references.

findings.title: Unsigned Proposals Rejected
findings.fact: Unsigned proposals or proposals signed by an individual not authorized to bind the prospective consultant will be considered nonresponsive and rejected.
findings.business_implication: The proposal must be properly signed by an authorized representative. Failure to do so will result in automatic rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the proposal includes a signature from an individual with authority to bind the company. Verify the signatory's authority and include the signature in the appropriate section (e.g., cover letter or signature page). Double-check before submission.

quotes.quote: Unsigned proposals or proposals signed by an individual not authorized to bind the prospective consultant will be considered nonresponsive and rejected.

findings.title: Conflict of Interest Disclosure Required
findings.fact: Proposers must include a Conflict of Interest Statement disclosing any financial, business, or other relationship with C/CAG that may impact the outcome of the contract, and list current clients who may have a financial interest in the outcome.
findings.business_implication: Failure to disclose conflicts or provide the required statement could lead to disqualification or termination of contract. It is a pass/fail criterion, so non-compliance is fatal.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review all relationships with C/CAG and current clients to identify any potential conflicts. Prepare a comprehensive Conflict of Interest Statement, including mitigation strategies if any conflicts exist, and ensure it is included in the proposal appendix.

quotes.quote: Include a Conflict of Interest Statement disclosing any financial, business or other relationship with C/CAG that may have an impact upon the outcome of the contract. List current clients who may have a financial interest in the outcome of this contract. Identify possible mitigation efforts, if any, to eliminate or avoid any actual or perceived conflicts of interest.

findings.title: Mandatory Federal Certifications and Forms
findings.fact: Proposals must contain specific federal certifications or forms: Certification Regarding Lobbying, Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility, and Voluntary Exclusion—Lower Tier Covered Transactions, and Disclosure of Lobbying Activities (SF-LLL) form.
findings.business_implication: Missing any of these mandatory federal forms will render the proposal non-responsive and lead to disqualification. This is a critical compliance requirement.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all three federal forms are completed using the latest versions and included in the proposal. Verify that the forms are properly signed and dated. Double-check the FHWA website for any updates before submission.

quotes.quote: Proposals must contain the following federal certifications or forms: (1) Certification Regarding Lobbying, (2) Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility, and Voluntary Exclusion—Lower Tier Covered Transactions, and (3) Disclosure of Lobbying Activities (SF-LLL) form.

findings.title: Incomplete Submittals Deemed Non-Responsive
findings.fact: An incomplete submittal will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff's discretion.
findings.business_implication: Any missing or incomplete required content can lead to immediate disqualification without evaluation. This is a high-risk area for proposal rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a compliance checklist based on the RFP requirements and use it to review the entire proposal before submission. Ensure all required sections, forms, and attachments are included and complete. Have a second person independently verify completeness.

quotes.quote: An incomplete submittal will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff’s discretion.

findings.title: Mandatory Proposal Content Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals that do not include the proposal content requirements identified within the RFP and subsequent addenda will be considered incomplete, rated a Fail, and receive no further consideration.
findings.business_implication: Failure to address every content requirement will result in a 'Fail' rating and elimination from the competition. This is a strict compliance gate.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully read the RFP and any addenda to identify all content requirements. Structure the proposal to explicitly address each item, using headings and cross-references. Conduct a final review to ensure no requirement is missed.

quotes.quote: Responses that do not include the proposal content requirements identified within this RFP and subsequent addenda and do not address each of the items listed below will be considered incomplete, be rated a Fail in the Evaluation Criteria and will receive no further consideration.

findings.title: References Requirement
findings.fact: Proposals must provide at least three references from agencies the proposer currently or has previously consulted for in the past three years.
findings.business_implication: Providing fewer than three references will make the proposal non-compliant and may lead to disqualification. References are also scored, so quality matters.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify at least three client references from the past three years who can speak to your firm's performance. Ensure their contact information is current and that they are willing to provide a positive reference. Include references for subcontractors if needed, but do not exceed five total.

quotes.quote: Provide as reference the names of at least three agencies you currently or have previously consulted for in the past three years.

findings.title: Insurance Acknowledgement Required
findings.fact: Proposers must submit a signed acknowledgement agreeing to provide required certificates of insurance within ten days of C/CAG's notice of selection.
findings.business_implication: Failure to submit the signed acknowledgement could render the proposal non-responsive, risking disqualification. Additionally, the requirement to provide insurance certificates within ten days of selection imposes a tight deadline, so the bidder must be prepared to secure the necessary insurance promptly.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the signed acknowledgement is included in the proposal package. Prepare in advance by identifying an insurance provider and understanding the minimum insurance requirements in Appendix D to be able to provide certificates within the ten-day window if selected.

quotes.quote: Submit a signed acknowledgement, for proposer only, that the proposer agrees to provide the required certificates of insurance providing verification of the minimum insurance requirements listed in Appendix D, Sample Agreement Template (see Section 11), within ten days of C/CAG’s notice to firm that it is the successful Proposer.

findings.title: Familiarity with Federally-Funded Projects
findings.fact: Consultant must demonstrate familiarity with providing services for federally-funded projects and have a clear understanding of requirements/needs to facilitate the project.
findings.business_implication: The evaluation will likely assess the bidder's experience with federal grants, including compliance with federal regulations. Lack of demonstrated familiarity could weaken the proposal's competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Highlight relevant experience with federally-funded projects in the proposal, providing specific examples and outlining understanding of federal requirements. Include resumes of key staff with such experience and any relevant certifications.

quotes.quote: Consultant shall demonstrate familiarity with providing services for federally-funded projects and have a clear understanding of requirements/needs to facilitate the project.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12:00 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Missing the deadline will likely result in the proposal being deemed non-responsive and rejected. Timely submission is critical.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit well before the deadline to avoid last-minute issues. Confirm the submission method (email to specified address) and ensure all requirements are met. Consider submitting a day early to mitigate any technical problems.

quotes.quote: Proposals are due: January 23, 2026, 12:00PM PST
Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, in accordance with the instructions contained in the RFP.

findings.title: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications
findings.fact: The deadline for requests for clarifications is January 9, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Any questions or clarifications must be submitted by this date. Missing this deadline may leave ambiguities unresolved, potentially affecting the proposal's quality.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit any clarification requests well before January 9, 2026. Keep a record of all communications and incorporate any clarifications into the proposal.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications: January 9, 2026

findings.title: Proposal Modification Deadline
findings.fact: Modified proposals must be received prior to January 23, 2026.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder needs to withdraw or modify a submitted proposal, the modification must be received before the submission deadline. This allows for corrections but requires careful timing.
findings.action_recommendation: If modifications are necessary, ensure they are submitted before the deadline. Keep track of the submission timeline and have a process in place to submit revised proposals promptly.

quotes.quote: To be considered for the project, however, a modified proposal must be received prior to January 23, 2026.

findings.title: Protest Deadlines for RFP Provisions
findings.fact: Objections to RFP provisions must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due.
findings.business_implication: The bidder has a very short window to challenge any perceived issues with the RFP terms before the proposal deadline. Missing this deadline could forfeit the right to protest, potentially locking the bidder into unfavorable terms.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly as soon as possible. If any provisions are considered arbitrary, biased, or unduly restrictive, prepare and submit a written protest before the deadline. Ensure the protest clearly describes the basis and proposed remedy.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due, for objections to RFP provisions.

findings.title: Protest Deadline for Non-Responsive Determination
findings.fact: Protests regarding non-responsive determination must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after notification.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder is deemed non-responsive or fails to meet minimum qualifications, there is a limited time to contest that decision. Missing this deadline could result in disqualification without recourse.
findings.action_recommendation: Monitor communications from C/CAG closely after submission. If notified of non-responsiveness, immediately prepare a protest with detailed justification and submit it before the deadline.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it did not meet the minimum qualifications or was found to be non-responsive.

findings.title: Protest Deadline for Award Recommendation
findings.fact: Protests regarding award recommendation must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after notification of non-selection or committee recommendation, whichever is later.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder is not selected, there is a short window to challenge the award decision. Missing this deadline could mean losing the opportunity to contest the outcome.
findings.action_recommendation: After notification of non-selection, immediately review the evaluation process. If grounds for protest exist, prepare a detailed protest and submit it before the deadline.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date on which the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or, if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later, for objections to the recommended award.

findings.title: Cost Proposal Requirements
findings.fact: The cost proposal must be detailed, task-based, using the Cost Proposal Template, including personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and other cost items, with a total cost summarized.
findings.business_implication: The cost proposal must be meticulously prepared to meet specific formatting and content requirements. Failure to comply could render the proposal non-responsive and lead to rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Use the provided Cost Proposal Template (Appendix C) and ensure all required details are included: personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and other costs. Double-check that the total cost is clearly summarized and that rates are fully loaded as defined.

quotes.quote: Provide a detailed task-based cost proposal for the project using the Cost Proposal Template (Appendix C). The cost estimate shall include personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and any other cost items necessary to perform each of the tasks listed in the Scope of Work. A total cost shall be summarized and presented.

findings.title: Indemnification for Public Records Act Release
findings.fact: By submitting materials, the proposer agrees to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of information under the Public Records Act.
findings.business_implication: The bidder waives confidentiality rights and assumes liability for any release of submitted materials under the Public Records Act. This could expose the bidder to financial risk if sensitive information is disclosed.
findings.action_recommendation: Before submitting, carefully review all materials for confidential or proprietary information. Consider marking sensitive documents, but be aware that the RFP states all submissions are public records. Assess the potential risks and ensure the indemnification obligation is acceptable.

quotes.quote: By submitting materials, (1) you consent to release of such materials by C/CAG if requested under the Public Records Act without further notice to you, and (2) you agree to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of such information.

findings.title: Termination for Conflict of Interest
findings.fact: C/CAG may terminate the contract if a conflict of interest is discovered and not properly notified.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure all potential conflicts of interest are disclosed upfront and any new conflicts are immediately reported to C/CAG. Failure to do so could result in termination for cause, damaging the bidder's reputation and financial standing.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a robust conflict of interest identification and reporting process. Train staff on the requirements and establish a clear protocol for notifying C/CAG of any conflicts that arise during the contract. Review the Conflict of Interest Statement in the proposal to ensure completeness.

quotes.quote: The C/CAG Project Manager may terminate the contract involving the conflict of interest and C/CAG may obtain the conflicted services in any way allowed by law.

Failure by the consultant to notify C/CAG Project Manager may be grounds for termination of the contract for cause pursuant to Section 4, Termination, of the Contract Agreement Template, provided as Appendix D to this RFP.

findings.title: Termination for Material Breach - Key Personnel
findings.fact: Removal of key personnel without prior written consent may be considered a material breach of contract, which could lead to termination.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that key personnel identified in the proposal remain committed to the project for its duration. Any changes to key personnel without C/CAG's approval could be deemed a material breach, leading to termination and potential legal consequences.
findings.action_recommendation: Secure commitments from key personnel to stay for the project duration. Develop a contingency plan for key personnel changes and seek C/CAG's written approval before any changes. Clearly communicate the importance of this requirement to the team.

quotes.quote: Removal of any key personnel identified in the responses to the RFP without prior written consent of C/CAG may be considered a material breach of contract.

findings.title: Contract Term Discrepancy
findings.fact: The RFP states the anticipated contract term is approximately 48 months, but also states the total contract duration shall be four (4) years, which is equivalent to 48 months. However, the schedule indicates completion by June 2030, which is more than 48 months from the expected start date of April 1, 2026.
findings.business_implication: There is ambiguity regarding the actual contract duration. If the contract is interpreted as 48 months from April 1, 2026, the end date would be March 31, 2030, but the RFP requires completion by June 30, 2030. This discrepancy could lead to disputes over the contract term and performance deadlines.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from C/CAG regarding the exact contract duration and end date. In the proposal, explicitly state the assumed contract term and completion date to avoid misunderstandings. Ensure the proposed schedule aligns with the latest completion date (June 30, 2030) to be safe.

quotes.quote: The anticipated contract term will be approximately 48 months.
The total contract duration shall be four (4) years; however, the e-bike white paper deliverable shall be completed and submitted for final approval no later than December 31, 2026.
C/CAG expects the work to commence on April 1, 2026 and to be completed no later than June 2030.

findings.title: Page Limit Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFP states that each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references. However, it also states that all required appendices and forms are excluded from the 20 page limit unless otherwise specified. This creates ambiguity about whether the supplemental materials (qualifications, project examples, work samples, references) are considered part of the 20-page limit or excluded as appendices.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity could lead to proposals being rejected for exceeding the page limit if the supplemental materials are counted. Conversely, if they are excluded, bidders might not include enough detail in the main body, potentially weakening their proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with C/CAG which sections count toward the 20-page limit. To be safe, keep the main body within 20 pages and place all supplemental materials in appendices. Ensure the proposal is compliant with the most restrictive interpretation to avoid disqualification.

quotes.quote: Each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references. All required appendices and forms are excluded from the 20 page limit unless otherwise specified.
As an appendix, include the following as documentation (no more than 5 pages) of relevant consultant information, qualifications, and experience:
